[[Image:ChancellorGeorge.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Dr. Thomas F. George]]
'''Thomas F. George''' is chancellor and professor of chemistry and physics at the [[University of Missouri-St. Louis]]. Born in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], George earned a bachelor of arts degree with a double major in chemistry and mathematics from [[Gettysburg College]] in [[Pennsylvania]], then a master of science and a doctor of philosophy degree in theoretical chemistry from [[Yale University]]. He was chancellor of the [[University of Wisconsin&ndash;Stevens Point]], before taking the St. Louis job in 2003,<ref>{{cite news |title=George Expected to be Named UM-St. Louis Chancellor |url=https://www.umsystem.edu/ums/news/news_releases/george_expected_to_be_named_um-st._louis_chancellor |access-date=10 March 2022 |issue=University of Missouri System}}</ref> and has announced his intention to retire from the University of Missouri-St. Louis in September, 2019.<ref name = "UMSL Chancellor to Retire in September">{{cite news|title= UMSL Chancellor Tom George to Retire in September | author = Petrin, Kae M. | date = March 21, 2019| publisher = St. Louis Public Radio | url = https://news.stlpublicradio.org/post/umsl-chancellor-tom-george-retire-september#stream/0 }}</ref> He is married to [[Barbara Harbach]], chair of the University of Missouri-St. Louis’s Department of Music, director of the university's School of Fine and Performing Arts, and Curators’ Distinguished Professor of Music.<ref name="UMSL Chancellor to Retire in September"/>
